name: Regional Human Anatomy
description: Regional anatomy of the limbs and trunk, including a brief introduction to the anatomy of the central nervous and cardiovascular systems. The course focuses on the bones, muscles, and neurovasculature of the limbs and trunk.
prerequisites: Corequisite: KIN 100L.

name: Regional Human Anatomy Laboratory
description: Laboratory accompanying KIN 100 focusing on regional human anatomy of the limbs and trunk.
prerequisites: Corequisite: KIN 100.

name: Biomechanics of Human Movement
description: Understanding of human movement from a mechanical perspective, enabling identification of injury risks, exercise prescription, and clinical evaluation concepts including functional anatomy, muscle and passive tissue mechanics, anthropometry, EMG, and linked-segment mechanics.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: PHYS 111; MATH 124 or MATH 127. Corequisite: KIN 121L (for Kinesiology majors).

name: Biomechanics of Human Movement Laboratory
description: Practical biomechanical tools complementing KIN 121 lectures.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: PHYS 111, KIN 104L; MATH 124 or MATH 127.

name: Advanced Biomechanics of Human Movement
description: Measurement, analytical and computational techniques for multi‑segment dynamic analysis of human activity; anthropometry, kinematics, kinetics, energetics, muscle mechanics, electromyography and applications in occupational, clinical, and athletic settings.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: KIN 121, KIN 121L. Corequisite: KIN 221L.

name: Advanced Biomechanics of Human Movement Laboratory
description: Laboratory supporting advanced biomechanical assessment from KIN 221.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: KIN 121, KIN 121L.

name: Fundamentals of Neuroscience
description: Introduction to the nervous system control of movement, cognition, and learning; basic neural structure and function.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: KIN 104. Corequisite: KIN 255L (for Kinesiology majors).

name: Fundamentals of Neuroscience Laboratory
description: Laboratory assessments of nervous system control of movement, cognition, and learning to support KIN 255.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: BIOL 273, PSYCH 101, KIN 104L.

name: Introduction to Neurological Disorders
description: Overview of selected neurological disorders and implications for physical activity.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: BIOL 273; Level at least 3A.

name: Task Analysis
description: Study of human task analysis with applications to movement, ergonomics, and performance.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: BIOL 273.

name: Musculoskeletal Injuries in Sport and Activity
description: Mechanisms of injury, tissue biomechanics, pathophysiology, assessment, management, and prevention of acute and chronic trauma in sport and activity.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: (KIN 100 and KIN 100L) or (BIOL 201/301); Level at least 3A Faculty of Health students.

name: Sensory Systems Neuroscience
description: Neural mechanisms of sensation with emphasis on systems relevant to human movement and perception.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: KIN 255 or PSYCH 261.

name: Neuromuscular Integration
description: Integration of neuromuscular physiology and control of human movement; applications to movement pathology and rehabilitation.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: BIOL 273 or PSYCH 261; Level at least 3A.

name: Occupational Biomechanics
description: Biomechanics of occupational tasks; measurement techniques; prevention of injury in workplaces.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: KIN 320.

name: Human Posture, Balance and Gait
description: Kinematics, kinetics, and neural control of standing, stepping, walking, and running; measurement and interpretation from biomechanical and neural perspectives; applications to aging and pathology.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: KIN 221 and KIN 221L.

name: Biomechanical Modelling
description: Quantitative measurement and analysis of the musculoskeletal system including multi‑segment dynamics, kinematics, kinetics, energetics, and EMG applications.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: KIN 221 and KIN 221L.

name: Chemistry Principles
description: Stoichiometry of compounds and reactions; periodicity and bonding; energy changes in chemical systems; electronic structure and reactivity; overview of organic functional groups and stereochemistry with biomedical examples.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Level at least 1B Biomedical Engineering.

name: Physiological and Biological Systems
description: Structure, functions, and properties of major biological systems (musculoskeletal, nervous, cardiovascular) in relation to design of biomedical devices; introduction to modelling; effects of pathology on device design.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Level at least 2B Biomedical Engineering. Antirequisite: SYDE 384/584.

name: Engineering Biology
description: Biochemistry and cell biology fundamentals including amino acids, carbohydrates, lipids, nucleic acids, proteins/enzymes, cell structure and metabolism with biomedical engineering examples.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Level at least 2A Biomedical Engineering.

name: Circuits, Instrumentation, and Measurements
description: Hardware measurement systems for biosignals: circuit analysis, first/second order responses, frequency response, operational amplifiers, signal conditioning, transducers, instrumentation amplifiers, A/D and D/A conversion; examples from EEG, ECG, EMG.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Level at least 2B Biomedical Engineering. Antirequisite: BME 392, SYDE 292.

name: Biomedical Engineering Design Workshop 2
description: First half of a two‑term capstone design project including prototyping and interim progress reporting; lectures on safety and risk analysis of biomedical technologies.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Level at least 4A Biomedical Engineering. Antirequisite: SYDE 461.

name: Biomedical Engineering Design Workshop 3
description: Conclusion of the fourth‑year Biomedical Engineering design workshop sequence.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: 4B Biomedical Engineering. Antirequisite: SYDE 462.

name: Biomechanics of Human Movement
description: Biomechanics of the musculoskeletal system including motor control and rehabilitation engineering; 2D/3D multibody models; muscle dynamics; applications to assistive devices, gait, occupational biomechanics.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Level at least 4A Biomedical or Systems Design Engineering.

name: Special Topics in Biomechanics
description: Selected topics at the undergraduate level in biofluid mechanics, tissue mechanics, sports engineering, and rehabilitation engineering.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Level at least 3A Biomedical Engineering.

name: Mechanics of Solids 3
description: Membrane stresses in shells; buckling; beams on elastic foundations; plane elasticity; torsion of non‑circular sections.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: CIVE 205; Level at least 3A Civil or Geological Engineering.

name: Civil Engineering Design Project 1
description: First term of the two‑term independent civil engineering capstone design project: problem identification, generation and selection of solutions, planning and time management.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: 4A Civil Engineering standing (departmental sequencing applies).

name: Civil Engineering Design Project 2
description: Continuation of CIVE 400 culminating in the final design of the proposed project.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: CIVE 400.

name: Transit Planning and Operations
description: Historical evolution of urban transit; mode technologies; vehicle motion models; transit travel time estimation under different regimes; scheduling; system performance measures; transit network planning objectives and methods.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Departmental standing (typically 4A/4B).

name: Engineering Biomechanics
description: Introduction to engineering technologies applicable to biomechanics, potentially including growth and form; biomaterials; gait kinematics and neurology; biotribology; joint anatomy, function and repair; occupational biomechanics; trauma prevention.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Level at least 4A in Biomedical, Mechanical, Mechatronics, or Systems Design Engineering. (Cross‑listed with ME 574).

name: Transit Planning and Operations
description: In‑depth exploration of transportation planning focused on public transit, including systems fundamentals, historical evolution, network/service planning, scheduling, operations, and performance measurement.
prerequisites: Upper‑year standing in Planning or permission of the school.

name: Contaminant Transport
description: Principles and modelling of contaminant transport processes in environmental systems (e.g., advection, dispersion, sorption, and reaction) with engineering applications.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Senior standing in Environmental or Civil Engineering (departmental lists apply).
